clue.text: X marks the scene of the dirty work

definitions.text: X marks the scene of the dirty work

parts.words: X marks the scene of the dirty work
parts.note: an X is the map sign for two roads meeting, and 'dirty work at the' such a junction is a stock phrase for skulduggery

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a crime-scene photo marked with an X; in fact the X is the shape of two roads crossing, and the idiom 'dirty work at the crossroads' supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An X is the conventional map symbol for an intersection where two roads cross.

clue.text: Foreign priest's remedy

definitions.meaning: a French parish priest, the counterpart of an English vicar

explanation.definitionFit: A French parish priest and a treatment that heals both take this spelling.

clue.text: Brooch might elicit this, if sat on

definitions.meaning: an old word for a clasp or jewelled brooch

definitions.text: might elicit this, if sat on
definitions.meaning: sitting on the pin of a brooch would draw a cry of pain

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a brooch is also the cry of pain from sitting on its pin.

clue.text: Worn, of course, for church parade

definitions.text: Worn, of course, for church parade

parts.words: Worn, of course, for church parade
parts.note: a church parade is soldiers marching to a church service, and they wear a standard uniform for it

explanation.walkthrough: Service dress is the army's everyday formal uniform; a church parade takes soldiers to a service, so the phrase has two meanings here.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers going to a church service on parade wear the army's formal uniform, named after its use in the forces.

clue.text: Roundheaded Muscovite embraces a nymph

parts.note: a round head is a round letter at the start, the letter O

indicators.note: embraces means the word for a Muscovite holds the article inside it

parts.note: a Muscovite stood for a Soviet citizen, a Red

explanation.surface: A Russian with a round head hugs a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: A round letter, O, heads RED, which embraces A to give O-RE-A-D. 'Roundheaded' also calls up Cromwell's Roundheads, which is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: An oread is a mountain nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: Frozen up and beaten on board with 10 per cent losses

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the word for frozen is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: iced means frozen
mated means beaten at chess, on the board

explanation.surface: A chess player, frozen and beaten, suffers heavy losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ICED into DECI. Decimate first meant to kill one soldier in every ten, so 'with 10 per cent losses' is the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman punishment killed one man in ten, so a decimated unit lost a tenth of its number.

clue.text: Musical group?

parts.note: the question mark hints at a second reading: a group of musicians, or a strip or ring of material

explanation.definitionFit: A group of musicians playing together is a band, and the query nods at the other sense, a strip or stripe.

clue.text: If a county has trouble with an ox, it will be an old English type

parts.note: the indefinite article a can be written an
Glos is the abbreviation for Gloucestershire, an English county

indicators.note: trouble means disturb or stir up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A farming county struggling with an ox turns out to be very old English.
explanation.walkthrough: AN and GLOS are followed by AXON, the anagram of AN OX made by 'trouble'. GLOS is the short form of Gloucestershire, a county in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Germanic people who settled England after the Romans left give their name to the English of before 1066.

clue.text: Object, East Cape. A very proper attitude

parts.note: to demur is to object
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness

explanation.surface: Someone protests about the Eastern Cape, taking a prim stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Cape' looks like a place in South Africa, but it is E and NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Demureness is modest, prim reserve, a very proper bearing.

clue.text: Feature of decimals, and of Nature expelled by Horace's fork

definitions.meaning: a decimal such as 0.333... has a digit or block of digits repeating without end

definitions.text: of Nature expelled by Horace's fork
definitions.meaning: Horace wrote 'Naturam expellas furca, tamen usque recurret': drive out nature with a pitchfork, yet it keeps coming back

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a quotation from the Roman poet Horace (Epistles I.10): what Nature does after a pitchfork drives it out is come back again.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating digits in a decimal and Nature's return after being driven out are both a coming back again.

clue.text: Love Magazine returned by ancient characters

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

indicators.note: returned means the short word for a magazine is turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: A copy of a magazine about love is sent back by someone in old-fashioned print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads the magazine word backwards after the O; 'Love' as a zero score in tennis is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham (also spelt ogam) is an early Irish alphabet of strokes cut on stones, so its letters are ancient characters.

clue.text: One scotch? A trap that might be calamitous

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A single whisky could be a trap leading to disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scotch' looks like whisky, but it is just letters: I, SCOTCH and A TRAP rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophic event is a disaster, so calamitous.

clue.text: What's wrong in the, bearing of military intelligence?

parts.note: military intelligence is MI, and 'of' makes it possessive, MI's
demeanour is one's bearing or manner

explanation.surface: A question about what is amiss in the way army spies carry themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue's ending as 'MI's demeanour': the possessive S joins MI to the word for bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeed or minor offence is something wrong that someone has done.

clue.text: Their place of work, the House of Commons

definitions.text: Their place of work, the House of Commons

parts.words: Their place of work, the House of Commons
parts.note: the parties not in government sit on the benches across from ministers in the chamber where MPs debate

explanation.walkthrough: The House of Commons is the elected chamber of the UK Parliament; the party facing the government sits there and its job is to oppose.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commons is where the parties out of government do their work of challenging ministers.

clue.text: What, a bathetic comedown !

parts.note: bathos is a sudden drop from the lofty to the trivial, and the clue's flat exclamation enacts such a letdown

explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is a ludicrous descent from the sublime, which is a letdown after a build-up.

clue.text: Writer takes exam without company at Whitsuntide

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, so a writer

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for exam wraps round the company abbreviation

parts.note: a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Someone sits a test on their own during the Whitsun holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside', so the exam word wraps the company. 'without company' looks like 'alone', but it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost is the Christian feast that the English call Whit Sunday, seven weeks after Easter.

clue.text: Watchful Franciscan friar

definitions.meaning: the ... were the branch of the Franciscans keeping the strict rule of St Francis

explanation.definitionFit: Alert and quick to notice is one sense; a member of the strict branch of the Franciscan order is the other.

clue.text: A man takes ono in forcefully

indicators.note: takes ... in means the words A man take a letter inside them

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man forcefully hauls someone in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes one in' puts I inside AMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Amain is an old word meaning with full force or vehemently.

clue.text: Odd, only one rose growing in a bed

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A strange sight: just a single rose flowering in the flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' is a flower in the surface but only fodder: I and ROSE rearrange. The bed is an osier bed, wet ground where willows are grown for basketry.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiers are willows planted in beds by rivers and cut for wicker, so they are things growing in a bed.

clue.text: It's anti-state to arrange one in old French currency

indicators.note: in means the arranging word and the numeral are placed inside the coin

parts.note: the sou was an old French coin, plural sous
to edit is to arrange or prepare text
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A rebellious act: rearranging the old French money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the editing word and the numeral inside the plural coin, which splits around them after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious talk or action stirs up rebellion against the government, so it is against the state.

clue.text: Work of Dulac, for example

definitions.meaning: Edmund Dulac was a French-born British book artist famous for pictures in fairy-tale books
an instance given to explain something, as in 'by way of'

explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Dulac (1882-1953) painted pictures for editions of fairy tales and the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture in a book and an example used to make a point both go by this word.

clue.text: Indicating the right quarter

parts.note: taken as written
a quarter is a point of the compass; E for east is one

explanation.surface: Someone points out exactly which part of town to go to.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes pointing out the right place, which is what the word does: 'over there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the word while pointing shows a direction or place, the correct spot.

clue.text: Seems a pirate's back here

indicators.note: back means the letters taken from the clue word are read in reverse
here means the letters are found within the word in front of it

explanation.surface: A pirate seems to have come back to this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside SEEMS sit the letters EEMS, and 'back' turns them round. Smee is Captain Hook's bosun in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is Captain Hook's boatswain in J M Barrie's Peter Pan, a pirate of the Jolly Roger.

clue.text: They were changed more than the usual once in the Cup Final

definitions.text: They were changed more than the usual once in the Cup Final

parts.words: They were changed more than the usual once in the Cup Final
parts.note: football teams swap halves of the pitch at half-time, and a match into extra time swaps again

explanation.walkthrough: The FA Cup Final is English football's showpiece match; a drawn game went to extra time, so the teams switched sides more than the usual single time.
explanation.definitionFit: The two halves of a football pitch that teams swap at half-time are named for each goal-line.

clue.text: La Peterson played a gentle musical role

definitions.text: La Peterson played a gentle musical role

parts.words: La Peterson played a gentle musical role
parts.note: the musical ... la Douce has a title character whose French name 'la Douce' means the sweet or gentle one

explanation.walkthrough: The musical is Irma la Douce (French, 'Irma the sweet'), staged in London in 1958; 'gentle' translates 'douce' and 'La' echoes the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of the musical Irma la Douce is the role, the 'gentle' one of the French title.

clue.text: Round the Orient catch upper-class types to convert

indicators.note: round means the word for catch goes around the abbreviation for the east

parts.note: taken as written
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E
men are types or chaps

explanation.surface: Missionaries go about the East netting posh people to win them over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' puts E inside the catch word. U for upper-class comes from 1950s British talk of 'U and non-U' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechumen is a convert being taught the faith before baptism.

clue.text: The one coming up to catch, about ten

indicators.note: about means the word for catch surrounds the numeral

parts.note: to net is to catch
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Someone is about to catch ten, waiting for whoever comes along.
explanation.walkthrough: NET goes about X.
explanation.definitionFit: The next one is the one following, the one about to come up.

clue.text: Patient carriers help to make a brick wall

definitions.meaning: litters on which the sick or injured are carried

definitions.text: help to make a brick wall
definitions.meaning: bricks laid lengthwise along the face of a wall, as opposed to headers laid end-on

explanation.definitionFit: Ambulance litters, and bricks laid with their long side showing in a wall, share this name.
